[USER] User asked about how different types of tea vary in terms of taste and flavor notes.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Different types of tea vary in taste and flavor notes based on factors such as the type of plant used, growing conditions, processing methods, and brewing techniques.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Black tea: Full-bodied and robust, with a strong, malty flavor and a brisk finish. May have notes of honey, fruit, or spice depending on the variety.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Green tea: Often described as grassy or vegetal, with a delicate, refreshing flavor and a slightly astringent finish. Can have floral, nutty, or sweet notes depending on the variety.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] White tea: Subtle and nuanced, with soft, floral notes and a sweet, lingering finish. May have hints of peach, honey, or apricot depending on the variety.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Oolong tea: Complex and aromatic, with a smooth, silky texture and a balance of floral, fruity, and toasty notes. Can vary widely in flavor depending on the level of oxidation.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Herbal tea: Made from non-tea plants like chamomile, mint, or rooibos, and can have a wide range of flavor profiles. Often described as soothing or calming, with flavors ranging from floral and earthy to sweet and spicy.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Overall, the taste and flavor of a tea will vary depending on factors such as its variety, origin, and brewing method.
